items.problem: Two consecutive build failures with CS0579 'Duplicate ...Attribute' errors (TargetFrameworkAttribute, AssemblyCompanyAttribute, AssemblyVersionAttribute, AssemblyConfigurationAttribute, AssemblyFileVersionAttribute, AssemblyProductAttribute, AssemblyTitleAttribute).
items.evidence: session-log.txt: 'Build failed with 4 error(s)' then 'Build failed with 6 error(s)'; error paths app\ActivitySensor\Tasks\obj\x64\Release\.NETCore,Version=v5.0.AssemblyAttributes.cs and obj\...\ActivitySensor.AssemblyInfo.cs.
items.skill_search: Grepped winui-uwp-migration for CS0579, AssemblyInfo, DefaultItemExcludes, GenerateAssemblyInfo, EnableDefaultCompileItems, 'Compile Remove', stale, nested project — no hits in SKILL.md or MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md; Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 copy step had no obj/bin guard.
items.root_cause: Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 step 1 copies every *.cs recursively from the UWP source with no bin/obj exclusion (that exclusion existed only in the later namespace-rewrite step). Stale UWP-era build artifacts — including obj\**\*.AssemblyInfo.cs and .NETCore,Version=v5.0.AssemblyAttributes.cs under a nested component/background-task subfolder — were copied into the project and compiled by the SDK default glob. The SDK only auto-excludes the project's OWN root obj/bin, not nested ones, so duplicate assembly attributes resulted.
items.proposed_fix: Apply the same bin/obj/.vs/.uwp-source/.git exclusion used by the namespace-rewrite step to the file-copy loop in Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 (Tier-1), and document the CS0579 cause/fix (delete stray nested obj/bin; DefaultItemExcludes=**/obj/**;**/bin/**; remove carried-over Properties\AssemblyInfo.cs) in MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md.
items.generalizes: Many UWP apps ship with checked-in or freshly-built obj/bin, and apps with a background task / Windows Runtime Component keep it in a NESTED subfolder whose obj is not covered by the SDK's default root-only exclusion. Any such app migrated by copying source files will hit CS0579 unless the copy excludes build dirs. This is a structural, scenario-independent defect in the migration tooling.
